No. SnoreSafe has no internet permission, so it can\'t send anything anywhere. Recordings and results stay on your phone, encrypted, unless you export or share them yourself.
A sound-recognition model runs on your phone and listens in short slices. It recognises snoring and about 30 other kinds of sound, such as talking, coughing, alarms, a crying baby or traffic.
Minutes of snoring per hour monitored, weighted by loudness: light counts once, loud twice and epic three times. It lets you compare nights of different lengths.
Where should I put my phone?
Face down on a bedside table, about an arm\'s length from your head, plugged in. Keep it in the same place each night so results are comparable.
Why did my session stop during the night?
Some phones stop apps to save battery. Open Battery settings from the home screen and let SnoreSafe run unrestricted. If it is stopped, SnoreSafe saves everything up to that point.
It counted my partner, fan or pet as snoring.
Lower the sensitivity in Settings, or turn off \"Count light snoring\". Placing the phone closer to you than to other sources also helps.
How much space do recordings use?
Clips are small. Full-night recording uses about 15 MB per hour. You can set a storage limit and how long audio is kept in Settings.
How do I move to a new phone?
Create a backup in Settings and save it somewhere you can reach from the new phone. Restore it there with the same password.
Can SnoreSafe tell me if I have sleep apnea?
No. SnoreSafe is a wellness tool and can\'t diagnose any condition. If you are worried about your sleep or breathing, talk to a doctor. You can share a PDF report with them.

SnoreSafe collects nothing.

• The app has no internet permission. It cannot send data anywhere.
• There are no accounts, ads, analytics or trackers.
• Audio is analysed on this phone. Recordings, results and notes are encrypted with a key kept in your phone's secure key store, inside the app's private storage.
• Nothing is included in your phone's cloud backup or copied to a new phone automatically.
• Data leaves the phone only when you choose to: a backup file, an export, or a report you share.
• Tips are handled by Google Play. SnoreSafe only learns that a tip was made, nothing about you.
• Uninstalling SnoreSafe deletes all of its data.

resources.string: Your phone has its own battery saver that can stop apps while you sleep. These steps stop it from cutting your night short.
Menu names vary between phones and Android versions. If a step doesn\'t match exactly, look for the closest option.

string-array.name: battery_steps_samsung
string-array.item: Open Settings → Battery → Background usage limits.
Make sure SnoreSafe isn\'t in \"Sleeping apps\" or \"Deep sleeping apps\".
Add SnoreSafe to \"Never sleeping apps\".
In Settings → Apps → SnoreSafe → Battery, choose \"Unrestricted\".

string-array.name: battery_steps_xiaomi
string-array.item: Open Settings → Apps → Manage apps → SnoreSafe.
Turn on \"Autostart\".
Tap \"Battery saver\" and choose \"No restrictions\".
In recent apps, lock SnoreSafe (long-press it and tap the lock) so it isn\'t cleared.

string-array.name: battery_steps_huawei_honor
string-array.item: Open Settings → Battery → App launch.
Find SnoreSafe and turn off \"Manage automatically\".
Turn on \"Auto-launch\", \"Secondary launch\" and \"Run in background\".

string-array.name: battery_steps_oneplus_oppo_realme
string-array.item: Open Settings → Apps → SnoreSafe → Battery usage.
Turn on \"Allow background activity\" (and \"Allow auto launch\" if shown), or choose \"Unrestricted\".
In recent apps, lock SnoreSafe so it isn\'t cleared.

string-array.name: battery_steps_vivo
string-array.item: Open Settings → Battery → Background power consumption management.
Allow SnoreSafe to run in the background.
In Settings → Apps → Autostart, allow SnoreSafe.

string-array.name: battery_steps_other
string-array.item: Open Settings → Apps → SnoreSafe → Battery.
Choose \"Unrestricted\" (on some phones, \"Don\'t optimise\").
While SnoreSafe is listening, don\'t swipe it away from recent apps.
